title: GET Routes and JSON Responses
summary: Create read-only routes that return predictable JSON resources and collections.

sketchBlocks.title: A GET collection route returns a predictable JSON array

tryItExercises.title: Return a club collection
tryItExercises.prompt: Add `GET /api/clubs` and return the provided `clubs` array with status `200` as JSON.
tryItExercises.hint: The route should use the existing collection rather than rebuilding it inside the handler.

help.concept: A collection GET route sends a deterministic array as a successful JSON response.
help.hint_1: Register the route with the read-method helper on the Express app.
help.hint_2: Chain an explicit success status with the JSON response method.

sketchBlocks.title: A specific path can return one JSON object

tryItExercises.title: Return a venue resource
tryItExercises.prompt: Add `GET /api/venues/3` and return the provided `venue` object with status `200` as JSON.
tryItExercises.hint: This exercise uses one fixed resource path; route parameters come next.

help.concept: A resource GET route can return one structured object with a predictable success status.
help.hint_1: Keep the provided object outside the handler.
help.hint_2: Use the same explicit status-and-JSON response pattern as the collection route.

sourceChecks.message: Return the venue as status-200 JSON.

quizDraft.title: Choose the structured response
quizDraft.prompt: Which response style directly sends a JavaScript collection as JSON with an explicit success status?
quizDraft.hint: Look for the response API that handles structured JavaScript data.

help.concept: Express can serialize JavaScript values with `res.json` while status remains explicit.
help.hint_1: The body in this question is an array, not plain display text.
help.hint_2: The successful status is part of the response contract too.

quizDraft.title: Recognize a predictable GET response
quizDraft.prompt: Which two choices strengthen a predictable beginner GET route?
quizDraft.hint: Focus on response status and body shape.

help.concept: A GET route contract is clearer when both status and JSON shape are deliberate.
help.hint_1: One correct choice concerns the HTTP status.
help.hint_2: Another concerns returning the intended resource data consistently.

options: Return a consistent JSON resource or collection shape.
Install a new package inside every route handler.
Change the collection into unrelated data on each request.

quizDraft.title: Name the collection shape
quizDraft.prompt: Complete the statement about a collection endpoint.
quizDraft.hint: Focus on whether the endpoint represents one resource or several resources returned together.

help.concept: Collection endpoints return several resources together in one structured JSON response.
help.hint_1: The missing term names the body shape used when multiple resources are grouped in one response.
help.hint_2: Contrast this collection response with the single-object resource response from the next sketch.

quizDraft.template: A route such as `/api/events` commonly returns a JSON [blank1] containing multiple event resources.

quizDraft.title: Trace a read-route response
quizDraft.prompt: Put these actions in the order a focused GET handler follows.
quizDraft.hint: The route must first be selected before its handler can build the response.

help.concept: A route moves from request matching to data selection to response construction.
help.hint_1: Start with the incoming request identity.
help.hint_2: Finish with the body being sent to the client.
